assessment: Re-verified all 60 pool cards under the standing tier-4 max-power mandate, and the old 'zero swaps' verdict does not survive the new charter: the pool holds two cards that are simply better than maindeck slots at the pilot's named table (Teferi, Hero of Dominaria over Secure the Wastes; Archmage's Charm over Ghostly Prison) plus two pod-conditional swaps the previous charter's conservatism left undocumented as swaps (Sphinx of the Final Word for permission pods, No More Lies for fast-combo pods). One factual correction to the previous pass: Monastery Mentor IS a payoff on the 004-verified loop's cast count — every Sol Ring/Signet recast is a noncreature spell — it is merely a slow one, and the correction changes reasoning, not his verdict. The remaining 54 cards are conditional tech, spare copies, and fair-deck filler, which is what this sideboard should be behind a verified, protected primary line.

swaps.when: Default 99 under the standing tier-4 max-power mandate — every pod
swaps.why: Teferi is the fourth sweep-surviving walker the v3 layer wants: his +1 draws while untapping two lands, so Counterspell/Swan Song mana stays open on the turns before the commit, and his -3 is the deck's only repeatable answer to a resolved artifact or enchantment besides Cyclonic Rift; Secure the Wastes needs seven-plus mana to present a clock that still crosses three combat steps against pods holding free interaction — mana the verified 15-cast kill (stack 006) simply wins with. Honest cost: the goldfish 'Win condition access' group loses its only unverified fair-combat member (5 cards to 4); the two verified lines plus Mystical Tutor and Jace, Wielder of Mysteries carry it.

citations.quote: buy resilience instead of restraint where you can — high toughness, indestructible and regeneration, token rebuilders, threats that replace themselves

swaps.when: Default 99 under the standing mandate — the pilot's named table (pods that mulligan well, hold free interaction, punish durdling) is control/combo-dense, where a third attack-tax is the deck's deadest card
swaps.why: Prison is the third redundant attack-tax (Propaganda and The Second Doctor's rider remain for the aggro seats) and blanks nothing at a draw-go table, while Charm is never dead: it guards a stack-006 window, steals an opposing Sol Ring (mana value 1) at rock-heavy bracket-4 tables, or draws two at end of turn under Heliod's discount. The {U}{U}{U} cost is real but the deck already supports {1}{U}{U}{U} Jace, Wielder of Mysteries on a 57-blue-pip base.

citations.quote: ask which of the opponent's likely cards your permanent invalidates, and which of yours are dead in this matchup; mulligan and sideboard decisions are largely virtual-advantage decisions

swaps.when: Pod-conditional: two or more heavy-permission blue seats at the table
swaps.why: Sphinx's static covers sorceries, so the second Approach of the Second Sun cast — the exact interaction window stack 002 walks — cannot be countered, and your held instants win any counter-war outright; Propaganda is near-dead at creature-light permission tables. It is explicitly not a Grand Abolisher substitute: a Reservoir activation is not a cast and artifact spells are outside its static, so it does nothing for the 006 windows.

citations.quote: assume every held answer appears the moment you present lethal, and count the table's open mana before committing

swaps.when: Pod-conditional: fast-combo or storm-dense pods where the game is decided by turn 5
swaps.why: The strategic frame's own vs-combo warning — the hug layer hands a storm pilot seven cards per spell — indicts Font of Mythos hardest: it is the slowest symmetric engine and pure fuel for their pilot, while a {W}{U} tax counter that exiles protects your turn-2-4 setup and beats recursion loops. The two-piece engine group thins from 10 to 9 in exactly the pods where the punisher clock is too slow to matter anyway.

citations.quote: McGuinness reports three mana as "essentially the most any player should pay for interaction" in cEDH

opens_lines.why_plausible: Every cast in the 004-verified mana-neutral loop is an artifact — a noncreature spell — so Mentor's trigger should produce arbitrarily many 1/1 prowess Monks in a single turn: a second payoff on the verified loop's cast count, correcting the previous pass's claim that none exists in the pool. Unwalked: the trigger arithmetic at scale, and whether a haste-less token army that must survive a full turn cycle of three opponents' interaction is a real win attempt next to the same-turn Reservoir kill.

Sphinx's static — instant and sorcery spells you control can't be countered — appears to close the counter-window stack 002 honestly walks on the second Approach cast; whether any non-counter interaction can still beat the second cast mid-resolution is the open question that decides how airtight the conditional swap makes plan B.

Jace's static replaces the empty-library draw with a win and a self-targeted Blue Sun's Zenith with X at library size presents that draw mid-resolution, before the shuffle-back instruction — but the layering of Archive's draw-doubling against Jace's win replacement, and what happens if Jace leaves the battlefield partway through, must be walked through. This scenario decides Laboratory Maniac's and Blue Sun's Zenith's entire sideboard value.

A free Approach under Omniscience is still cast from hand, Heliod's per-opponent-draw discount plus table-draw density can realistically pay {7}{U}{U}{U}, and free countermagic then defends the second cast. Unverified: cast-from-hand satisfaction under an alternative cost, the win-check timing, and the cost that every X-spell resolves at X=0 when cast free under it.

Fraying Sanity triggers at the beginning of the end step, before cleanup discards happen, so whether Fruition-bloated trim-to-7 discards ever count (including via a repeated cleanup under CR 514.3) is a genuine open rules question that decides whether the curse doubles the punisher engine or misses it entirely.

No sac outlet or counters theme to feed it, and its death payout is thopters that die to the next sweeper — including your own planned Supreme Verdict.

Its Birds trigger on instants and sorceries only — zero triggers across an unbounded 006 loop turn of artifact casts — and the token board dies to your own Supreme Verdict.

X mana to stun one creature is single-target tempo the plan doesn't want; the deck answers creatures with Supreme Verdict and exile, not turn-loans.

The most on-plan bench card that still doesn't fit: {1}{U} instant that hands opponents six cards on your turn — a {6}-discount Heliod ritual — but the maindeck already carries ten symmetric engines; first in line if an engine slot ever opens.
The opponent controls the repetition, so a professional opponent gives you the minimum and stops; it is a politics tool that selectively feeds one seat, not an engine.
Five mana, one creature, your end step only: Loran is the sole maindeck ETB worth rebuying, and Displacer Kitten already re-triggers her on every noncreature cast.
Both abilities restrict the mana to instant or sorcery spells — illegal for every artifact cast in the 004/006 engine, and awkward even fairly in a permanent-heavy engine deck.
Sixth X-draw behind Stroke of Genius, Braingeyser, Prosperity, Skyscribing and Mathemagics; instant speed is real but it displaces nothing those five don't already cover.
Spare physical copy — the maindeck already runs Stroke of Genius and singleton bars a second.

Opus triggers on instant and sorcery casts only, so an unbounded 006 loop turn gives it zero pumps. Correction to the previous pass: the pool DOES hold a second loop-cast payoff — Monastery Mentor — but Virtuoso still isn't it.
Draws only when a creature entered under you last turn, and this deck deploys creatures in ones — most upkeeps she is a sub-seven-devotion statue that isn't even a creature.
{2} per exile with everything returning only on sacrifice: the pieces it 'protects' are off the battlefield when the loop needs them, and Teferi's Protection does the sweep-dodge in one card.
Six mana to draw two and stun two creatures is a full commit turn spent on an effect Cyclonic Rift embarrasses for two.
Never dead at the mandated table where Ghostly Prison usually is: counter a 006-window threat, steal an opposing Sol Ring, or end-of-turn draw two under Heliod's discount — see swap 2.
Improvise applies to nonartifact spells and pays generic only: it cannot cast a single loop piece and cannot pay the deck's 57 blue pips — the two jobs this deck actually has for mana.

Pod-conditional counter-war tech (swap 3, two-plus permission seats); explicitly not an Abolisher backup — a Reservoir activation is not a cast, and the 006 artifact casts are outside its instant/sorcery static.
Ninth-choice permission: the five free/cheap counters plus Counterspell, Dovin's Veto and (conditionally) No More Lies and Archmage's Charm all outrank it, and it answers no creature.

Three shuffle effects (Flooded Strand, Mystical Tutor, Long-Term Plans) is too thin to un-stick Brainstorm's put-backs in a 99; its one live trick — drawing the card Long-Term Plans buried third from the top, at instant speed — is not worth a slot alone.

The verified 006 kill means the deck doesn't need a second, unverified nine-mana package — a slot on Omniscience displaces a card supporting the proven line. Re-argue only if the Approach-under-Omniscience scenario verifies favourably.
Four mana (three on defense) to loan a creature back with library-topping the owner chooses; the maindeck answer suite exiles or sweeps instead of loaning tempo.

Redundancy for the still-unverified Jace, Wielder empty-library line: until that scenario passes he is a 2/2 with no other function that dies to any removal mid-draw, and even after it he enters behind Jace, who draws cards on his own.
A +1/+1-counters voltron plan this deck doesn't run; no verified or candidate line touches him and his army-pump has almost no army to pump.
Two life and a death cantrip is draft rate; every maindeck three-drop compounds an engine instead of replacing itself once.
A 2/1 flying cantrip; this deck's card advantage is engines, not one-shot ETB bodies, and it feeds no verified line.
Same card as Cloudkin Seer a mana worse for the colour: a one-shot cantrip body in an engine deck.
The corrected-build exile stands: seven mana for one theft, and the draw-three rider needs three stolen permanents the deck has no other way to accumulate.
The corrected-build exile stands: it grows into exactly the creature your own Supreme Verdict plan kills, and the Squid payout dies to the next wipe as well.
The corrected-build exile stands: {X}{W}{W} fair tokens are the White Sun's Zenith problem again — a combat board walked straight into your own planned Verdict, on the deck's weaker colour.
Even at five-plus graveyard card types she is a 6-8 mana fair threat off both verified axes, and the Mindslaver trigger hands the punished player an extra turn to untangle.

Ten mana, and the hand-size clause actively fights the deck: opponents discarding to nothing blanks Iron Maiden, Ebony Owl Netsuke and Viseling — and its layering against your own Folio of Fancies' 'no maximum hand size' is an open rules question besides.
Twelve mana, and its theft trigger needs opponents to sacrifice nontoken permanents — nothing in the 99 forces a sacrifice.

Mill-two-per-draw is not a believable clock into three 99-card libraries at a professional table, it feeds graveyard pilots, and the punisher plan wants opponents' hands full, not their libraries empty.
Its end-step trigger resolves before cleanup discards happen, so whether Fruition-bloated trim-to-7 discards ever count is an open rules question (see opens_lines) that decides its entire value here.
Pod-conditional (swap 4): the best cheap setup protection against fast pods, but at grindy tables the {3} tax stops mattering by mid-game, which keeps it out of the default 99.

The mana engine it wants was refuted: 004 verified the loop mana-neutral and 005 refuted the mana-positive extension, so there is no infinite colourless to feed it — and {4} per counter is fair-deck rate.

The corrected-build exile stands: instant-speed Cats are the most Verdict-shaped wincon in the pool, and wincon access is now carried by two verified lines, Mystical Tutor and Jace, Wielder of Mysteries.
Pure redundancy for the unverified Jace, Wielder empty-library line, and Stroke of Genius already fills that job for one fewer blue pip; re-argue only if that scenario passes.
The third flash grant behind Heliod's back face and Leyline of Anticipation, covering only sorceries — and the Ring rider is untriggerable: no card in the 99 tempts.
Covers only Hullbreaker Horror of the four 006 pieces — Sol Ring, Arcane Signet and the Reservoir cannot hold it — while Grand Abolisher closes every window wholesale for the same two mana.

Enters tapped, so by the 004 ledger's requirement — each recast covered by same-turn production — every Hullbreaker rebuy cycle pays {3} for mana that arrives a turn late, strictly mana-negative; outside the loop it is the slowest rock on a 57-blue-pip base.

Goldfish land-drop hit rate is 57.2% at t5 and 48.2% at t6 — exactly the engine turns — so it pays opponents more reliably than it pays you; maindeck Jace Beleren draws everyone unconditionally and survives the artifact sweep.
{4} in and {C}{C} out makes each loop recast minus-two by the 004 ledger's arithmetic, and its draw rider needs an X-spell cast the same turn — the loop casts none.

Corrected reasoning, same verdict: Mentor IS a payoff on the 004-verified loop — every artifact cast is a noncreature spell, so an unbounded loop turn makes unbounded prowess Monks — but the tokens have no haste, so the kill waits a full turn cycle behind interaction the same-turn Reservoir line never exposes, and the Monks die to your own Supreme Verdict. Revisit only if the Mentor-loop scenario verifies a protected next-turn kill worth a slot.

gaps: No Grand Abolisher redundancy exists anywhere in the pool: no other card restricts what opponents may do during your turn, so the verified kill's one shield still has no backup — acquiring one is outside this analysis's constraint and remains the deck's one structural exposure.

The Abolisher-closes-006 claim still has no checker-passed walkthrough; the channel-land loophole (Otawara activates from a card in hand, not from an artifact, creature, or enchantment) is the specific thing a scenario must scope before the shield is played as airtight.

The two-piece rate (41.3% by t6) cannot be raised from this pool: it contains zero hand-size punisher effects, and the only mill-adjacent candidates (Teferi's Tutelage, Fraying Sanity) attack a different axis.

The Monastery Mentor loop-payoff line needs a stack scenario before his verdict could flip, and the strategy corpus has no section on whether a haste-less token win attempt surviving a full multiplayer turn cycle is ever preferable to a same-turn kill.

Jin-Gitaxias's hand-size reduction against your own Folio of Fancies' 'no maximum hand size' is an unresolved layering question — one more reason his verdict rests on the punisher anti-synergy rather than on rules certainty.

The strategy corpus still lacks sections on group-hug/forced-draw punisher archetypes and empty-library win lines (per strategic_frame.gaps), so several judgments above rest on oracle text, the six verified stacks, and the v3 goldfish rather than citable principles.
